subject.title: [Feature]: Support external unified session storage for stateless session mode

question: Should OpenClaw pursue external shared session storage for multi-instance deployments, and should that backend boundary live in core, a plugin API, or deployment guidance after the SQLite/session-accessor work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the backend ownership, credentials/secret model, consistency semantics, migration path, and interaction with planned SQLite/database-abstraction work are product and architecture choices.

options.title: Design backend-neutral session storage
options.body: Define a core or plugin-facing contract for session metadata, transcripts, lifecycle cleanup, migration, credentials, and consistency before selecting Redis, MongoDB, Postgres, or another implementation.

options.title: Defer until database abstraction settles
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for the SQLite/session-accessor and broader networked database direction to settle before designing the session-specific backend.

options.title: Document external deployment only
options.body: Keep OpenClaw local-state-first for now and document sticky sessions, external orchestration, or third-party plugins as the supported multi-instance pattern.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral session storage
recommendation.body: Define a core or plugin-facing contract for session metadata, transcripts, lifecycle cleanup, migration, credentials, and consistency before selecting Redis, MongoDB, Postgres, or another implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh Lehman has the strongest direct history on the session/transcript storage migration that this backend design would build on.
